title: IFTTT alternatives, with checked prices | 50agents
description: IFTTT alternatives: Apple Shortcuts for your iPhone, Home Assistant for a local smart home, Zapier or Make for work apps, 50agents for email chores.
answer: For automations on your iPhone, Apple Shortcuts already runs them on your device; for a smart home you control locally, Home Assistant lists 1,600+ integrations and keeps your data at home.
If you have moved on to work apps, Zapier and Make have free plans with multi-step workflows, and 50agents builds an AI agent for chores like drafting email replies from plain words.
ask: Go through my unread email now, then every weekday at 8:00, and draft replies
lede: IFTTT is cheap and simple, and for many people it is enough; people leave when the free plan's hourly checks or one-step Applets get in the way.

entries.suits: People who use IFTTT for admin and want more judgement than an Applet has, such as drafting replies to unread email each morning, sending nothing without a yes.
entries.limit: No smart-home devices, no phone app and no location triggers. It works with web apps, not your lights or your thermostat.

entries.suits: iPhone and iPad owners. Automations start from things only your phone knows: the time of day, arriving at a place, opening an app.
entries.price: Apple's own app on iPhone and iPad
entries.limit: Automations are "specific to a device", so they run on your phone, not in the cloud while it is off.

entries.suits: Smart-home fans who want everything to run at home, without a cloud, with automations such as lights on at sunset.
entries.price: Open source; you run it on a device at home
entries.limit: You run it yourself on a device at home, so setup and updates are your job.

entries.suits: People who moved from personal to work automations and need the long tail of business apps: 10,541+.
entries.price: Free: 100 tasks a month. Professional: $19.99 a month billed yearly (750 tasks)
entries.limit: The free plan is 100 tasks a month and two-step Zaps only, less than IFTTT's free 1,000 credits.

entries.suits: Tinkerers who want longer, branching workflows on a visual canvas, with a free plan of 1,000 credits a month.
entries.price: Free: 1,000 credits a month. Core: from $9 a month (10,000 credits)
entries.limit: Most actions cost a credit each, so a long workflow uses the free credits faster than a one-step Applet.

us: Your Applets have moved from your phone and home to work apps like Gmail, Sheets and Slack.
The job needs judgement each time, such as which emails need a reply and what to say.
You want anything sent to other people to wait for your yes.
them: Your automations involve smart-home devices or your phone. IFTTT covers both, with apps for iOS and Android.
Your Applets are one step and an hour's delay is fine. The free plan, with unlimited Applets, is hard to beat.
You want it cheap: Starter is $25.08 a year and Pro is $65.88 a year.

move.title: Sort Applets by where they run
move.body: Phone and location ones go to Shortcuts, device ones to Home Assistant or stay on IFTTT, and web-app ones to a work automation tool.

move.title: Note each Applet's trigger and action
move.body: We found no Applet export on IFTTT's own pages, so write them down: "If new email from X, then add a row to my sheet".

move.title: Rebuild the web-app ones in plain words
move.body: In 50agents you can type the Applet as you wrote it; Captain turns it into an automation and asks which sheet or which inbox.

move.title: Turn off, then delete
move.body: Turn each Applet off once its replacement has run for a week.

faqs.q: Is there a free alternative to IFTTT?
faqs.a: Yes. Make (1,000 credits a month) and Zapier (100 tasks a month) have free plans, and 50agents is free to start. Home Assistant is open source, and Apple Shortcuts is Apple's own app on iPhone and iPad.

faqs.q: What is the best IFTTT alternative for a smart home?
faqs.a: Home Assistant, if you are happy to run it at home: 1,600+ integrations and local control.

faqs.q: How much does IFTTT cost now?
faqs.a: Free gives 1,000 credits a month with hourly checks. Starter is $2.09 a month, billed $25.08 yearly, with 15-minute checks, and Pro is $5.49 a month, billed $65.88 yearly.
